buttonLabel: "Explore journeys through Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil and Peru combine Rio de Janeiro's ocean beaches, Iguaçu Falls, ancient Cusco and Machu Picchu. Flights between Brazil's coast and the Peruvian Andes are best planned with ample connection time. Before choosing an itinerary, consider the rainy season in each region, gradual acclimatization to altitude, Machu Picchu admission tickets and payment arrangements in two different currencies.
---

## Brazil and Peru: why combine these countries?

In [Brazil](/brazil/), journeys often revolve around [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the ocean and [Iguaçu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In [Peru](/peru/), the main attractions are quite different: [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and, on longer programs, [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). One journey can reveal tropical landscapes, the Pacific Ocean and monuments of the Inca civilization.

It is best to plan the route in stages. Brazil's cities and resorts are a long way from the Andes. There is no short tourist transfer between Rio and Peru's Cusco: one or more flights are required, often with an airport change somewhere along the transport chain. In Peru, the high-altitude section begins after coastal [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), and travelers need time to adjust.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Options include programs devoted specifically to Brazil and Peru, as well as routes with Argentina, Chile and other principal countries. Check the total number of countries before booking: an additional country brings another logistical stage and separate immigration formalities.

## Choosing between Rio, Iguaçu, beaches and Machu Picchu

For a first major journey covering both countries, two questions are a useful starting point. Do you want to see **both sides of Iguaçu Falls**, and how many days do you want to devote to **Peru's historic sites**? If ocean relaxation appeals, you can finish the itinerary in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). If Andean culture is the greater draw, allow extra time for Cusco and the Sacred Valley.

| Option | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Brazil + Peru | Rio, Iguaçu, Machu Picchu |
| With a beach section | Extra days in Búzios |
| New Year journey | A celebration in Rio, followed by Peru |
| With Argentina | Another urban or nature-focused section |

The current [13-day Peru and Brazil: Machu Picchu, Rio and Beaches itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) begins in Lima, continues through Cusco and Titicaca, then visits the Brazilian side of Iguaçu, Rio and Búzios. Mountains, waterfalls and beaches are spread across different days on this program; they are not a handful of stops in a single city.

[Brazil and Peru at New Year](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/) puts the celebration on Copacabana at the beginning, then takes travelers to Peru's monuments, Paracas and the Nazca Lines. The holiday date determines the order: moving the December section to any other month would change the tour's defining feature.

The [15-day Brazil, Peru and Argentina group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) includes Rio, Iguaçu, Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu, followed by an Argentine section with Buenos Aires and the Perito Moreno Glacier. This is a journey through **three countries**, with its own duration and logistics.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_v_peru_i_braziliyu,tour_source_braziliya_i_peru_na_novyj_god,tour_brazil_peru_argentina_group_15_days}}

The choice often becomes clearer after counting **full sightseeing days**, rather than only the total duration. One part of a program may involve multiple transfers, while another includes relaxed time at the beach. Compare how much time is genuinely available at Machu Picchu, Iguaçu and the ocean.

## Getting from Brazil to Peru

The countries share a land border in the Amazon, including the crossing between Assis Brasil and Iñapari. But it lies far from the classic Rio–Iguaçu–Lima–Cusco routes. For most trips involving these attractions, **flying is more practical than a long overland journey** across the western Amazon.

One commonly used air corridor passes through **São Paulo and Lima**. From Lima, travelers usually take a flight to Cusco or begin an overland program along the Peruvian coast. Specific nonstop routes, departure days and ticket availability change, so connection times and airports must be checked for the actual travel dates. A transfer through a third country also requires checking transit rules based on nationality.

If the Brazilian section includes Iguaçu, do not treat [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) as an international air hub offering direct service to every region of Peru. Routes often involve a major airport and a separate domestic flight or connection. Compare not just the ticket price but the length of the layover, whether baggage must be collected, any terminal changes and travel time from the hotel.

For flights, **baggage on every segment** must comply with each carrier's actual fare conditions. One leg may allow a suitcase while another charges for an extra piece or imposes a lower hand-luggage limit. Tickets bought on separate reservations require additional connection time: an airline is not automatically obliged to protect a separately booked onward flight.

## From sea level to the Andes: handling altitude

Rio and Lima are close to sea level, while **Cusco stands at approximately 3,350 meters**. If you were swimming at the beach yesterday and fly into a high-altitude city today, your body faces an abrupt change in conditions. Some excursions go even higher: the Lake Titicaca area lies at about 3,800 meters.

A calm first day and a sensible pace are helpful at altitude. Avoid heavy exertion in the first hours. Headaches, nausea, unusual weakness and worsening symptoms after ascending require attention; if symptoms intensify, do not continue gaining altitude according to schedule without medical assessment. Travelers with chronic heart and lung conditions should discuss the journey with a doctor in advance.

Some travelers prefer to spend their first high-altitude night below central Cusco, in the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), before traveling to Machu Picchu. This is a planning option, not a universal guarantee of acclimatization. Rearranging days is possible only after considering admission tickets, trains, accommodation and the actual tour program.

Choose travel insurance according to altitude and activities, not just the countries listed on the policy. Standard city-trip coverage may exclude certain high-altitude routes or active excursions.

## Machu Picchu tickets and time for travel within Peru

A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is tied to **a specific entry circuit, date and time**, and available slots are limited. It is therefore best to organize the visit around a confirmed ticket, then coordinate the train, transfers through Aguas Calientes, overnight stay and return journey.

The Cusco region has many attractions, but even nearby sites require their own time. Visits to the Sacred Valley, Sacsayhuamán and the city's historic center should not be crammed into a single short day without checking excursion durations. If the aim is a deeper understanding of ancient Peru, removing an optional stop in Brazil makes more sense than trying to see everything in one morning.

When the journey includes [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), an additional overland stage is needed between Cusco and the lake. It should be counted in the overall duration. Comparing Ada Tours itineraries shows that some finish the Peruvian section after Machu Picchu, while others continue toward Titicaca or Paracas.

## Seasons: Brazil and Peru rarely follow the same calendar

In Rio, Southern Hemisphere summer months, roughly December to March, are usually hot and humid. This is the season of beaches, major festivities and heavy downpours. Weather at Iguaçu Falls also changes with the seasons; water volume and access to some walking areas depend on current conditions.

In the Peruvian Andes, **the dry season is generally May through October**. Walks around Cusco and Machu Picchu may be more comfortable then, although nights are colder. The rainy season can complicate rail, walking and road sections, so precise dates and contingency time matter more than the simplistic notion that Peru is always warm.

| Region | Practical guide |
|---|---|
| Rio and Búzios | Heat and summer downpours |
| Iguaçu | Water levels and trail conditions |
| Cusco and Machu Picchu | Dry season for walks |
| Lima | Coastal weather |

Lima's coastal climate is different from the mountains: a cool, overcast sky by the sea does not mean Cusco has the same temperature. Travelers may need beachwear, comfortable boots and a warm jacket within the same week. Visiting the Amazon adds an even hotter and more humid section.

When choosing dates, identify **your main experience**. If New Year's in Rio is the priority, the Peruvian part should be fitted around that celebration; for long walks at Machu Picchu, travelers often aim for the Andean dry months. Both are possible, but expectations of the weather are different.

## Documents and entry: Russian citizens

**According to official information checked on October 15, 2026**, Russians holding a valid ordinary international passport can make short tourist visits **to Brazil and Peru without a visa**, subject to a **90-day limit within the relevant 180-day period** for each country. Crossing the border of one does not count as entry to the other: immigration procedures and permitted stays are separate.

Before departure, check the current rules for each participant's nationality, required passport validity, itinerary documents and connection rules. A tour including Argentina requires a separate check for [Argentina](/argentina/). If a flight transits through a third country, visa-free access to Brazil and Peru **does not automatically extend to transit** there.

On an international journey, distinguish an airline ticket, permission to enter a country and confirmed admission to a tourist attraction. Even when no visa is required, an airline seat and a Machu Picchu time slot must be booked separately. Minors may be subject to additional border-crossing requirements under their nationality's rules.

## Currencies, cash and Russian-issued bank cards

Brazil uses the **Brazilian real (BRL)** and Peru the **Peruvian sol (PEN)**. One country's currency should not be treated as ordinary legal tender in the other. US dollars are sometimes convenient for exchange or as a reserve budget, but you cannot be certain of paying for a taxi, small purchases or local tickets in dollars.

**Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not work abroad.** If you hold a card from a bank in another country, check the issuer and the ability to pay and withdraw cash in both countries. Cards are more common in tourist districts and major cities than in small communities, while private drivers and markets may mainly accept local cash.

It is useful to divide the estimated budget into services already included, meals paid for independently, optional excursions, local transport, admission tickets, tips and contingency expenses. Whether each item is included depends on the actual program; the tour's title alone does not determine it.

## Time zones, flights and luggage

Rio de Janeiro is normally **two hours ahead of Lima**. But Brazil spans other time zones as well, so the time of each flight segment should be checked for its actual departure city. Tickets show the airport's local time, while a phone calendar may display times differently when crossing borders.

Many logistical problems on a multi-country trip arise where one transport leg ends and the next begins. An example is a flight from Rio via São Paulo to Lima, followed by a separate domestic service to Cusco. Consider passport control, baggage collection and re-check-in, minimum connection times and possible delays to the first flight.

Clothing has to work in different climates. Rio calls for lightweight beachwear; Iguaçu requires protection from moisture; Cusco needs warm layers and sun protection at altitude. It is easier to check baggage weight and the number of bags across all tickets before departure than to discover restrictions when transferring to a local airline.

## How Ada Tours helps combine the two countries

When planning a trip, we compare current programs, establish which places are included and coordinate a logical sequence of days. When linking Brazil and Peru, it is especially useful to decide where to place the international flight, how much time to allow at altitude, which Machu Picchu admission slot is needed and whether to add beach days.

If the journey is tied to New Year, start with the holiday date and confirmed flights. If Machu Picchu is the goal, tickets and an appropriate visiting time take priority. A route including a third country requires separate checks of its entry rules, air connections and actual stops, so an appealing list of countries does not turn into a tour of airports.

In the [general multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/), you can compare other combinations. Here you can choose a program in which Brazil and Peru are genuinely part of the main route.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I travel overland from Rio to Cusco?

Brazil and Peru are theoretically connected by a land border, but from Rio or Iguaçu to Cusco it is a very long journey through other regions. For a standard tourist itinerary, flights through major air hubs such as São Paulo and Lima, followed by a separate leg to Cusco, are more practical.

### How many days are needed for Rio, Iguaçu and Machu Picchu?

A program of approximately 12–13 days or more is a useful starting point, accounting for international and domestic flights. The [13-day Peru and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) includes these attractions and beach time in Búzios. A shorter itinerary would mean dropping some stops.

### Do Russian citizens need visas for both countries?

For short tourist trips with a valid ordinary Russian international passport, according to official information dated October 15, 2026, Brazil and Peru allow visa-free entry within the applicable 90-day limits over 180 days. Transit and additional country rules must be checked separately.

### Is it better to start with Brazil's beaches or Peru?

Both orders are possible. If high-altitude Cusco follows an ocean holiday, allow time to adjust to altitude. If the trip centers on New Year's Eve on Copacabana, the Brazilian section should align with the celebration date. The final decision depends on flights, the season and the itinerary.

### Can I pay for everything with one Russian bank card?

No. Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards do not work abroad. Travelers need verified foreign payment methods and a reserve of local cash: reals in Brazil and soles in Peru.

### Can Machu Picchu be visited on any free day?

Admission requires a ticket for a particular circuit, date and time. The journey from Cusco and train schedules need to be coordinated with that slot. During busy periods, suitable tickets should be purchased in advance.

## Adventures between Brazil and Peru: what the journey really involves

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose principal geography includes both Brazil and Peru and whose overall itinerary has a substantial adventure theme. **These are not direct two-country hiking expeditions from Brazil to Peru.** Relevant programs travel through Argentina, Chile and Bolivia, combining flights, overland transfers, 4×4 vehicles and historical excursions.

The combination is appealing for its contrasts: around [Iguaçu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) there are humid forests and walking paths, in the Andes there are dry highlands, and at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) an archaeological complex among mountain slopes. The length of the journey is determined not by the distance between two country names but by the sequence of actual stops and high-altitude transfers.

To compare programs without a thematic filter, open [tours through Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/brazil_peru/). Separate collections of [adventures in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/) and [adventures in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/) help you compare other options in each country.

## Brazil: waterfalls, walking routes and the beginning of the journey

On the [18-day five-country program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the Brazilian days take in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Foz do Iguaçu. In Rio, visits to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain are scheduled: these are viewpoints and city excursions. At Iguaçu, travelers follow established paths to the falls, while some additional activities, such as the Macuco Safari boat ride, are booked separately.

This section offers memorable natural experiences, but **it should not be treated as a multi-day trek, a jungle expedition or a guaranteed rafting adventure**. A standard waterfall excursion and an independent sporting activity require different preparation and carry different restrictions. If you want an active program specifically in Brazil, check the named activity, its duration and terms in the chosen tour.

After the Brazilian section, the itineraries cross the border near Iguaçu and continue through Argentina and Chile. These stages cannot be omitted when assessing duration and difficulty: they take actual days and include separate flights.

## Where the demanding section lies: the Atacama and Bolivian Altiplano

On the current extended programs, the main off-road section starts after [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. Travelers then cross Bolivia in 4×4 vehicles, visiting [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), high-altitude landscapes, geothermal fields, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

This is a substantial part of the adventure content, although **it is located in neither Brazil nor Peru**. The thematic label applies to the whole multi-day product, while the catalog shows an intersection of its principal countries. The distinction is especially important for anyone seeking a strictly Peruvian trek or an active route through Brazilian parks.

The high-altitude journey differs from a walk at Iguaçu in temperature, remoteness, road quality and possible effects of altitude. The 18-day tour includes a specific acclimatization stop before the Bolivian section. Travelers need warm layers, sun protection and a discussion of their tolerance for high elevations before setting off. This section cannot be shortened without changing the itinerary itself.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

After Bolivia, the route continues toward Puno and Lake Titicaca, then to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), finishing in Lima. This section combines mountain roads, high-altitude cities, historic monuments and visits to Inca heritage sites.

**Visiting Machu Picchu is not equivalent to a multi-day hike on the Inca Trail.** The 18-day program describes access to the complex involving a train journey. If you want a sporting trek, nights in tents or a special trekking permit, look for those as a separate product rather than assuming their inclusion from the words Machu Picchu alone.

An important question is how much time is allowed in and around Cusco. A tightly scheduled route through five to eight countries may introduce the main monuments without necessarily including several free days for independent mountain hikes. Decide in advance what matters more: covering a wide geography or spending longer in a particular part of the Andes.

## Comparing extended journeys through Brazil and Peru

| Program | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Five countries, 18 days | Iguaçu, Atacama, Uyuni, Machu Picchu |
| Six countries, 20 days | Uruguay is added |
| Eight countries, 32 days | Includes the Galápagos and Colombia |

The [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) already covers varied natural zones and the principal off-road section. The [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds Montevideo and other stops. The [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues through Ecuador to the Galápagos and Colombia. This is a significantly longer route with more domestic flights.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Base your choice on four factors: full days at key sites, the altitude of overnight stays, the proportion of travel time and the actual types of activities. An off-road drive across the Altiplano, a walk to a waterfall and a Machu Picchu excursion involve different levels of exertion, although all can form part of the same adventure journey.

## Borders, flights and equipment: preparing for the trip

Brazil's lowland sections have a humid, hot climate; the high-altitude areas of Chile, Bolivia and Peru can bring cold, strong winds and intense sunshine. Light clothing alone will not suffice for the whole tour. Comfortable shoes are needed for long excursions and uneven paths, but specialist trekking gear is required only for a particular scheduled activity.

A multi-country itinerary involves numerous entry and exit formalities, flights and overland transfers. Visa and document requirements depend on citizenship, while baggage restrictions depend on the chosen airlines. We help coordinate the country sequence, flights and arrangements for overland travel in advance. Medical questions, including whether high-altitude travel is suitable, must be addressed individually before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Brazil and Peru

### Is there a two-country Brazil–Peru trek in the selection?

The relevant published tours also include other principal countries. The key off-road section lies in the Atacama and Bolivian Altiplano region; it cannot be represented as a direct trail between Brazil and Peru.

### Is a hike on the Inca Trail included?

Mentioning Machu Picchu does not confirm that. On the featured 18-day tour, access to the complex includes a train, while a specialist walking trek must be checked separately against the program.

### Which section requires special attention to altitude?

The transfers from Chile into Bolivia and stays at high elevations, followed by the Peruvian section around Puno and Cusco. Plan acclimatization and assess personal limitations before traveling.

### Can I keep Machu Picchu but visit fewer countries?

That would require a separately designed itinerary. Compare existing [Peru itineraries](/peru/tour/) with the full [catalog of journeys through Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/brazil_peru/), then discuss the stops you want.

  On the itinerary through Peru and Brazil, the beach portion is concentrated in the Brazilian resort of Búzios. Travelers first discover Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca, then continue to Iguaçu Falls, visit Rio de Janeiro and finish their journey with time on Atlantic beaches. Find out where there is free time by the sea and where the coast is simply part of a city excursion.

## Peru and Brazil: where the beach holiday fits into this itinerary

This selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} involving Brazil and Peru. Its centerpiece is the [13-day journey Peru with Machu Picchu and Brazil with the beaches of Búzios](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/). The route combines Andean history, natural attractions and several final days on Brazil's coast.

The term 'beach holiday' refers primarily to time in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/) on the Atlantic Ocean. The Peruvian section includes coastal Lima, but its principal excursions take place in the city before the route climbs to the highlands around Cusco and Machu Picchu. The itinerary does not include a separate multi-day stay at a Peruvian seaside resort.

| Section | Planned activities |
|---|---|
| Peru: Lima | Historic center, Miraflores and Pacific Ocean views |
| Peru: Cusco, Machu Picchu, Titicaca | Ancient history and high-altitude excursions |
| Brazil: Iguaçu | Waterfalls and national park |
| Brazil: Rio de Janeiro | Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, city panoramas |
| Brazil: Búzios | Beach resort and a free day |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_v_peru_i_braziliyu}}

That is why this trip is a good choice for travelers who want to finish an active sightseeing itinerary with time by the ocean, rather than spend their entire vacation in one beachfront hotel.

## Lima: the Pacific Ocean without a separate resort program

The first days are spent in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). The city stands on the Pacific coast, but its characteristic views feature high coastal cliffs, urban neighborhoods and pedestrian spaces overlooking the water. The excursion includes a stop at Miraflores' Park of Love, home to Víctor Delfín's sculpture *The Kiss*.

Sightseeing continues through the historic center and the Larco Museum. Lima has a rich food scene and cultural life of its own, but on this trip the ocean primarily provides dramatic urban panoramas.

A stay at a serviced beach, swimming and surfing lessons are not listed as separate paid services in the Peruvian section. Seeing the ocean from the seafront is a wonderful beginning to the journey, but the day is a city experience rather than a beach holiday.

## Cusco and Machu Picchu: exchanging the ocean coast for the Andes

After Lima, the route heads to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), approximately 3,400 meters above sea level. Acclimatization and visits to archaeological monuments are scheduled here. The following day, travelers take a train to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), where terraces and buildings from the Inca civilization survive.

The itinerary then continues with a bus excursion to Puno and a visit to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), including the floating Uros Islands. Water returns as a theme, but now it is associated with a high-altitude lake, local traditions and sightseeing. Titicaca should not be presented as a beach alternative to Brazil's ocean resort.

The altitude difference between Lima and the Andes is considerable. When planning the full trip, preserve the time allowed for acclimatization and do not imagine the first six days to be a relaxed seaside vacation.

## Iguaçu: waterfalls before heading for the coast

On day 7, travelers fly from Lima to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The following day is devoted to the Brazilian side of the falls: walking along the canyon, viewing platforms and panoramas of the powerful cascades.

Iguaçu is a major natural part of the journey, but it lies inland rather than on the ocean coast. Spray from the waterfalls and the surrounding tropical forest offer a completely different experience from swimming at a beach. Plan these days with comfortable footwear and protection for electronic equipment against water, without allocating beach time.

A flight then takes the group to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), where famous sea views and green mountains above the bays appear.

## Rio de Janeiro: the ocean as part of the cityscape

In Rio, the itinerary includes a visit to Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. From above, travelers see the ocean, city, beaches and islands. The scheduled sightseeing days themselves, however, are occupied by excursions and transfers.

Even staying near the sea does not necessarily mean having a full beach day. Hotel location, excursion hours and driving times all matter. If extra hours on Copacabana or Ipanema are essential to your holiday, discuss them separately.

After exploring Rio, the route heads north to Búzios, which becomes the main seaside section of the whole itinerary.

## Búzios: the main beach portion of the trip

On day 11, the itinerary includes a transfer from Rio to [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/), approximately 180 kilometers to the north. Once a fishing village, it has become a resort with small bays, beaches, restaurants and streets suited to strolling.

Day 12 is reserved for free time. The itinerary lists possible activities available at the resort: beach relaxation, swimming, boat trips, surfing, kayaking, scuba diving and other water sports. **A list of local possibilities does not mean that every activity is included in the tour price.** Arrangements, schedules, weather limitations and payment for any particular activity should be confirmed in advance.

You can choose a quiet bay, spend the day exploring on foot or book a boat excursion according to your preferences. When choosing a beach, consider wind, water conditions and safety. The appeal of Búzios is that there is finally time to enjoy the resort without a compulsory multi-stop sightseeing program.

Day 13 includes breakfast and a transfer to the airport. Thus the full free beach day on the published schedule is day 12, not three final days entirely free of commitments.

## Choosing the balance between sightseeing and beaches

This itinerary makes particular sense for a first trip to South America: Peru's main cultural attractions, Iguaçu and Rio are complemented by Atlantic beach time. But the actual balance is a substantial sightseeing section followed by a short beach finale in Búzios.

If you want more days by the water, discuss extending the resort stay before booking flights. If particular water sports matter to you, confirm age and medical restrictions, instructor availability and what is included in advance. Swimming and boat trips are weather-dependent.

Compare [all Brazil + Peru itineraries](/multi-country/brazil_peru/), [beach holidays in Brazil](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/) and [multi-country journeys with beach time](/multi-country/interests/beach-holidays/). They offer other balances of seaside days without assuming that services are included on the current tour.

## Frequently asked questions about beach holidays in Brazil and Peru

### Where exactly is the free beach day scheduled?

In Búzios, on day 12. The transfer from Rio takes place on day 11, and day 13 is reserved for the airport transfer.

### Is there a beach holiday in Peru?

On the current tour, Peru is represented by Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Puno and Lake Titicaca. Lima's ocean views are part of a city tour; no separate resort section on the Peruvian coast is advertised.

### Is scuba diving in Búzios included in the tour price?

Scuba diving is listed among activities available at the resort. Its arrangements and payment are not confirmed as an included service, so these must be discussed separately.

### Can I extend my stay in Búzios?

You can discuss a custom extension, with adjustments to transfers, hotel arrangements and the return flight. This is not automatically included in the 13-day itinerary described.

## Cultural tours in Brazil and Peru: bringing two different histories together

**The main appeal of combining Brazil and Peru is the striking contrast between their cultural experiences.** In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travelers discover the historic center, squares, churches, city life and Brazilian traditions. In Peru, the historical journey continues through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/): Inca archaeological monuments stand alongside colonial-era buildings.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries as principal destinations and a cultural and historical theme. Some programs also include Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and other countries. Selecting two countries means they both appear on the route, but it does not guarantee a direct flight from Brazil to Peru or an equal number of days in each.

The main options appear in the [Brazil + Peru catalog](/multi-country/brazil_peru/). Here we compare their historical sightseeing days and substantial excursions. For cultural itineraries through additional countries, see [multi-country cultural tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Brazil: Rio and urban culture, not Inca archaeology

On the Brazilian section of many programs, the main destination is [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Here visitors can explore old neighborhoods, historic buildings and city squares, visit famous viewpoints and discover the city's culture. The specific places and excursions vary between tours.

For example, on the [15-day New Year journey through Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/), Rio's historic center, Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado are scheduled before the flight to Lima. The festive days focus on the city's atmosphere, while the principal archaeological section begins in Peru. Carnival or New Year celebrations must not be assumed to be part of every cultural tour: specific dates and an appropriate itinerary are required.

Some routes also include [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The falls add a natural experience, but seeing the cascades is not in itself an excursion into Brazilian history. If vacation time is limited, decide what matters more: extra time in historic Rio or a separate visit to Iguaçu.

## Peru: Lima, Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu

[Lima](/peru/place/lima/) provides an introduction to the Spanish colonial period through central squares, churches, administrative buildings and museums. Some itineraries add older urban sites and collections from pre-Columbian cultures. For example, the [13-day Peru and Brazil journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) includes Lima's historic center and the Larco Museum.

The route then climbs to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the former capital of the Inca Empire. What matters here is the transition between eras: Inca stonework, [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/) and other ancient structures stand alongside colonial churches. A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) completes this historical sequence, with terraces and residential buildings integrated into the Andean landscape.

On the [14-day Brazil, Argentina and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), the Peruvian section covers Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Titicaca. But this tour includes **a third principal country, Argentina**, with Buenos Aires and waterfalls on the other side of the border. It is chosen for a broad overview of South America, not to maximize time in Peruvian museums.

## How much time to allow for historical excursions

A museum, a city tour and an archaeological complex require different arrangements. In Rio, it is better to allow separate time for the historic center rather than combining it with several distant viewpoints. In Lima, museum visits and sightseeing in the center can complement each other if travel times are accounted for.

The most time-sensitive section is [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The journey between them involves transport coordinated with tickets, entry times and a specific sightseeing circuit inside the archaeological complex. Visitors cannot freely substitute any date and admission time on arrival. These components should be booked before optional additional excursions.

Cusco lies at a considerable altitude, so a packed first day after a flight from a coastal city will not suit everyone. Coordinating the pace and overnight stays directly affects the enjoyment of the historic walks.

## What the combination adds, and what the transfers take away

Peru alone offers enough to explore Inca civilization in depth. Adding Brazil brings a very different urban and cultural setting, the ocean coast and a possible nature stop at Iguaçu. The cost of that variety is international flights and time spent at airports. Adding Argentina or Chile broadens the cultural experience further but complicates the schedule.

For a deeper exploration of Peruvian history, consider [culture-and-history tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/); to discover Brazilian cities and traditions, see [cultural tours in Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/). A multi-country program is better for travelers who deliberately want to combine two different cultural regions in one trip.

We help compare existing itineraries, coordinate flights, the sequence of excursions and time to adjust to altitude. Questions about specific admission tickets, guide languages and included services are resolved according to the selected tour, without automatically applying one program's conditions to another.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural tours in Brazil and Peru

### Can I combine Rio de Janeiro and Machu Picchu in one journey?

Yes. For example, the [13-day Peru and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) includes Peru's historical highlights and Rio. It also makes other stops, so compare the full duration and the days spent in each city.

### Which country is more interesting for ancient history: Brazil or Peru?

On these itineraries, the principal focus on Inca history and earlier Andean cultures is in Peru: [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The Brazilian section introduces primarily historic Rio and its local urban culture.

### Does a cultural tour include Iguaçu Falls?

Not every tour does. Iguaçu is part of the [14-day itinerary via Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/); other programs may have a different set of nature stops.

### Do I need to buy Machu Picchu admission in advance?

Yes, the visit to the archaeological complex should be planned around tickets available for the required date, time and circuit. We coordinate the itinerary, and the exact entry rules are checked before booking.

### Do all tours in this selection visit only two countries?

No. The catalog also includes journeys on which Brazil and Peru are two of several principal countries. The [14-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), for instance, also visits Argentina.

## A festive journey through Brazil and Peru: where the main event takes place

[Brazil](/brazil/) and [Peru](/peru/) can combine two very different parts of a journey. [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) offers New Year's Eve by the ocean or Carnival performances at the Sambadrome. Peru continues the route toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and, on some programs, [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/).

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries among the principal destinations and an events theme. **The celebration is scheduled in Brazil, while subsequent sightseeing days take place in Peru.** Peru's presence in this themed selection does not imply attendance at Inti Raymi, a local carnival or another festival there.

## New Year in Rio: a 15-day trip or a longer itinerary

The most direct option is the [Brazil and Peru New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/). The program begins in Rio in late December. After visits to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain, New Year's Eve celebrations are scheduled for December 31 on Copacabana; a free day for rest follows. The itinerary then continues to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Cusco, Puno, Paracas and Nazca. A separate New Year's dinner at the hotel carries an additional charge: it is optional, not a mandatory part of the beach celebration.

The [19-day New Year journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) also celebrates December 31 in Rio, but after Brazil it visits Argentina, Chile and Bolivia before Peru. This is an option for those who want to see Iguazú, the Atacama and Uyuni after the festivities. When comparing it with the 15-day itinerary, remember that additional countries mean different flights, mountain sections and fewer free days at each stage.

In both cases, **the holiday determines the beginning of the journey**. If spending New Year's Eve in Rio is your main motivation, arrivals and hotel dates must be planned around December 31 rather than trying to move the event to the end of the trip.

## Carnival and the Champions Parade: how two programs differ

The [18-day program featuring the Champions Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) is specifically built around performances by the winning samba schools at the Sambadrome. This is the central festive event in Rio, after which the journey continues through Argentina, Chile and Bolivia to Peru. Tickets for the Champions Parade are included; the seating sector and conditions must be checked for the specific departure.

[Another five-country tour during Carnival](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) includes a Carnival visit to the Sambadrome in Rio, followed by Iguazú, Buenos Aires, Santiago, the Bolivian lagoons and Peru's monuments. It is designed as an extended continental journey, not just several days in Brazil and Peru.

When choosing between the Carnival programs, confirm **the exact performance date and format**, the ticket category and the included transfer. Carnival and the Champions Parade are related but occupy different parts of the festive calendar. The general name 'Carnival tour' is not enough to treat the offers as identical.

## Why the Peruvian section requires a different pace

Moving from nighttime festivities in Rio to the Andes changes the physical demands. Coastal [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) is near sea level, while Cusco lies at approximately 3,350 meters and Titicaca above 3,800 meters. After flying, allow real time for rest and gradual acclimatization, especially if high-altitude excursions lie ahead.

On the 15-day two-country tour, Rio is followed by a gradual Peruvian route from the capital to the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu, then Puno and back to the coast. On the five-country programs, high-altitude Bolivia precedes the Peruvian days; the planning challenge is different there: coordinating several mountain sections and overland transfers without unnecessary haste.

For other options, see the [general Brazil and Peru travel selection](/multi-country/brazil_peru/). For programs built around celebrations in any of the countries visited, explore [multi-country event tours](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/) or [event-themed itineraries involving Brazil](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/).

## Details to agree in advance

Before booking, check exactly when the Carnival performance or New Year's Eve celebration is scheduled, what the ticket includes, how transport to the venue is arranged and how much free time remains afterward. In Peru, important details include train dates and Machu Picchu admission, logistics around Cusco and Titicaca, and the conditions of specific flights. A five-country itinerary also involves additional borders, climate zones and connections.

We help build the journey around the selected event, coordinate hotels, guides and transfers, clarify travel documents for each traveler's nationality and plan a comfortable pace in the Andes. Admission to a specific festival, ticket prices and included services are always determined by the actual program, not merely the name of the selection.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours in Brazil and Peru

### Do travelers celebrate New Year in Peru?

On the New Year programs described, the celebration takes place on Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro. Peru comes later in the itinerary, in January.

### Can Rio Carnival and Machu Picchu be combined on one trip?

Yes. One example is the [18-day Champions Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/). Additional principal countries lie between Rio and Peru, so this is an extended continental journey.

### Is a separate Carnival program in Peru needed?

Not for these tours: the main event is in Brazil. The Peruvian section includes cities and natural and historical attractions, but none of the listed itineraries advertises a separate festival in Peru.

### What should I choose for a celebration and Peru without three additional countries?

The [Brazil–Peru New Year program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-new-year/): it combines the principal festive event directly with the following itinerary through Peru. The Carnival offers listed cover the broader geography of five countries.
